questions.title: Ball hits your golf bag by accident
questions.question: You hit your ball and it bumps into your own golf bag. What do you do?

choices.text: Add a penalty and hit again from the same place.
Play the ball from where it stopped, no penalty.
Pick up the ball and drop it close to the bag.
Move your bag and hit the shot again.

questions.explanation: If your ball hits your bag or anything you are carrying and it was an accident, you just play the ball from where it stops. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Extra points added to your score for breaking a rule.

vocabulary.term: Play the ball from where it stops
vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Hit the ball from the place it finishes after you hit it.

questions.teachingTip: Show what happens if the ball hits a bag or towel—let children see they just play from there. Ask them what to do and let them practise.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they must always take a penalty if their ball hits their bag.
Some may try to drop the ball or hit again instead of just playing from where it stopped.

questions.title: Ball hits player's own equipment
questions.question: If you hit a shot and your ball accidentally hits your own golf bag, what should you do under the Rules?

choices.text: Add one penalty stroke and replay the shot.
Play the ball from where it comes to rest, with no penalty.
Pick up the ball and drop it as close as possible to the bag.
Move your bag and replay the shot.

questions.explanation: According to the Rules, if your ball in motion accidentally hits your own equipment, you must play the ball as it lies without penalty.
